title: Intervention at Delegation: Can Permission Scoping at Sub-Agent Creation Time Prevent Irreversible Actions?

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Compelling chain: implement least-privilege delegation -> measure irreversible action rate, success rate, and false-blocking rate -> quantify safety/utility tradeoff. Addresses a critical problem (principle of least privilege) recognized by NIST, with all intermediate metrics independently valuable.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires implementing a delegation framework with three permission levels and running 20 tasks. Framework setup (tool access scoping) is moderately complex but uses established patterns. Beginners would need mentor guidance on the framework.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable: three permission levels x 20 tasks with three clear metrics. The comparison is well-defined and the first milestone (full vs. minimal permission comparison) stands on its own.
